title: Measuring climate credibility? Talk, emissions, and corporate debt composition
abstract: arXiv:2611.25951v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We examine whether a directional measure that compares emissions growth with earlier climate discussion is associated with corporate debt composition. The analysis links earnings-call climate language, LSEG/Refinitiv emissions, Capital IQ debt shares, RepRisk incidents, and accounting information for public firms over 2010--2021. The Emissions-to-Talk Index (ETI) is the central empirical measure, but we describe it literally rather than treating it as a general indicator of disclosure quality. In the baseline industry-and-year fixed-effect specification, a higher ETI is associated with a lower bank-debt share. The estimate falls by about four-fifths and is statistically insignificant when firm and year fixed effects are used on the same observations. translated_title: 衡量气候可信度？言论、排放与企业债务构成
translated_abstract: 我们研究了一种将排放增长与早期气候讨论进行比较的方向性指标是否与企业债务构成相关。该分析将2010至2021年间上市公司的业绩电话会议气候语言、LSEG/Refinitiv排放数据、Capital IQ债务份额、RepRisk事件以及会计信息联系起来。排放与言论指数（ETI）是核心实证指标，但我们仅对其进行字面描述，而非将其视为披露质量的通用指标。在基准的行业与年份固定效应设定中，较高的ETI与较低的银行债务份额相关。然而，当在同一观测样本上使用公司与年份固定效应时，该估计值下降约五分之四且在统计上不再显著。当使用完整指数预测下一日历年度的债务构成时，结果同样不显著。基于言论与排放独立组成部分以及无比率中间设定的结果……
tldr: 本文构建排放与言论指数（ETI）以检验企业气候言论与后续排放增长的关系，发现ETI与银行债务份额的负相关性在公司固定效应下大幅减弱且不显著，表明该指标对企业债务构成的解释力缺乏稳健性。
en_tdlr: This paper constructs an Emissions-to-Talk Index (ETI) to examine whether firms' climate talk precedes emissions growth, and finds its negative association with bank-debt share becomes statistically insignificant under firm fixed effects, suggesting limited robustness of the index's link to corporate debt composition.
